A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpinQuant. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–C are readable and can be matched despite conference reformatting and additional appendix experiments.

before.justification: V3 reports original quantization experiments on LLaMA and Mistral models, including perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, ablations, latency measurements and signal-to-noise analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds instruction-tuned model evaluations, further quantization comparisons, optimization-time comparisons and end-to-end GPU measurements.

M1.justification: The learned R1/R2 rotations, Cayley SGD optimization, optional online Hadamard R3/R4 rotations and GPTQ integration remain unchanged. The additional experiments do not introduce a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Appendix A.10 and Table 18 add MMLU and TLDR9+ summarization evaluations using instruction-finetuned LLaMA-3.2 1B/3B models. These introduce few-shot task coverage beyond the retained WikiText2 and eight zero-shot commonsense benchmarks.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets remain intact. Table 17 adds a dedicated weight-only comparison with RTN, SmoothQuant, GPTQ and AWQ, extending beyond v3's weight-only rotation-initialization study. Table 15 additionally makes GPTQ an optimization-time comparator; no new baseline algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: New protocols include five-shot MMLU accuracy and one-shot TLDR9+ test ROUGE-L. GPU evaluation changes from component-level decoding profiling to W-FP8/A-FP8 end-to-end TTFT/TTIT measurements with and without Hadamard rotations at batch sizes 1, 8 and 32 and sequence length 4096. Weight-only evaluation also expands across model sizes. Existing Section 4.1 optimization settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 16 extends existing RTN-versus-GPTQ analysis with LLaMA-2 13B/70B RTN results, and Table 15 adds comparative optimization-cost analysis. Controlled GPU timings replace the component breakdown. Earlier initialization, calibration, clipping, gradient and signal-to-noise analyses remain.

E5.justification: The 100-trial random-rotation study and uncertainty values in Tables 3, 4, 11 and 12 are retained. The added tables report point estimates without introducing new seed counts, confidence intervals or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 14–18 add timing, weight-only, few-shot and additional RTN results. For example, new LLaMA-3.2 1B MMLU accuracy is 47.3 for SpinQuant, 43.4 for vanilla RTN and 49.3 for BF16; TLDR9+ ROUGE-L is 16.7, 14.9 and 16.8 respectively. Tables 1–13 retain their values. V3's component-level GPU results are removed, while its SNR results reappear unchanged as Table 19.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, rotational-invariance reasoning, the Stiefel-manifold optimization formulation and Appendix B.1's gradient analysis are retained. No new theorem, assumption, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about learned rotations, robustness, GPTQ compatibility and quantization accuracy. The abstract's added code link does not change those claims.

C2.justification: Appendices A.7–A.8 add an explicit argument that optimization cost is worthwhile and attribute most accuracy gains to learned rotations, with GPTQ providing an incremental benefit. A.6 discusses low GPU overhead conditional on optimized kernels. Existing mechanism explanations and future-research qualifications remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds a project code-availability link and identifies the GPU implementation's FBGEMM FP8 GEMM, epilogue-fused dequantization and Tensor Core Hadamard kernel, with source links. Table 15 adds GPTQ optimization times while redisplaying previously reported SpinQuant times. These are documentation additions, not evidence that the underlying method changed.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning remain unchanged. Numeric citations become author-year citations, with corresponding bibliographic formatting and disambiguation changes.

P1.justification: V4 adopts ICLR headings and author-year citations, updates acknowledgments, expands A.6 and adds subsections A.7–A.10. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact, without extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation expands substantially: the GPU component pie chart and latency list are replaced by a paired TTFT/TTIT table, and four additional tables present optimization costs, RTN/GPTQ comparisons, weight-only results and instruction-tuned evaluations. Existing SNR and distribution figures are retained with relocation or renumbering. The conference template also changes title styling, headers and typography.

improvement.justification: The added instruction-tuned evaluations, broader ablations, controlled end-to-end GPU timings and code/kernel disclosures provide useful incremental validation and reproducibility information. The core method and main results remain unchanged. Benefits are tempered by losing the component-level timing breakdown and by overstatement in A.9: Table 17 provides AWQ perplexities but no AWQ accuracy values supporting its accuracy claim.
